Advantech separates robot safety from AI in a five-layer platform

Its IGX Thor-based MIC-735-IT supports an optional Safety MCU and engineering evidence; final system certification remains application-specific.

PR Newswire ↗22 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A platform spanning the robot lifecycle

Advantech presents five layers: perception, AI computing and motion control, functional safety, production and validation, and deployment and management. The architecture aims to help robot builders integrate hardware, software and validation evidence.

An independent safety path

AI computation is separated from health monitoring and fault detection to support application-defined safe states. The NVIDIA IGX Thor-based MIC-735-IT can include a Renesas Safety MCU. Diagnostics, a safety manual and FMEDA-related evidence support engineering work.

System certification remains specific

Support for standards such as IEC 61508 and ISO 13849 does not certify every robot built on the platform. Integrators or customers remain responsible for hazard analysis, integration, validation and final certification. Advantech plans demonstrations at NVIDIA GTC Berlin.
